--- title: "[Graph.select_edges_by_id()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Select edges by their IDs. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L10795-L10881){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.select_edges_by_id(edge_ids) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Select edges by id](/assets/graphs/select-edges-by-id.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="A six-node grid whose seven edges are labeled with their integer ids 1 to 7. After select_edges_by_id with ids 2 and 5, the edges B–C and C–F are selected and drawn in the accent color." width="100%"} Adds the given edges to the current edge selection. Edge IDs are internal integer identifiers assigned when edges are created; they can be listed with `get_edge_ids()`, read from the `id` column of `get_edge_df()`, or obtained from methods that return edge IDs. Use this when you already know exactly which edges you want to act on, for example to: - turn the output of a query or a filtered edge DataFrame into a selection for `set_edge_attrs_ws()`, `delete_edges_ws()`, or `rev_edge_dir_ws()` - re-apply a selection saved earlier with `get_selected_edge_ids()` Selection is cumulative: the IDs are added to whatever is already selected and duplicates are ignored; call `clear_selection()` first to replace the selection. Edge and node selections are independent, so the node selection is untouched. The graph is modified in place and returned for chaining. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [edge_ids]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A list of integer edge IDs to add to the selection. Every ID must belong to an existing edge; a missing ID raises `KeyError`. IDs are processed in order, so valid IDs that come before the missing one are still selected when the error is raised. An empty list is allowed and leaves the selection unchanged. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The same graph (modified in place) for method chaining. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [KeyError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If any edge ID doesn't exist in the graph. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Edge IDs are assigned in creation order, so the first two IDs in this triangle belong to `A-B` and `B-C`. Selecting them leaves `C-A` unselected: ::: {#c1bd2605 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A")]) ) edge_ids = graph.get_edge_ids() graph.select_edges_by_id(edge_ids=[edge_ids[0], edge_ids[1]]) graph.count_selected_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 2 ``` ::: ::: A common pattern is to filter the edge DataFrame with Polars and pass the matching IDs back in. Here the edges heavier than `1.0` are selected and then shown with `get_edge_df_ws()`: ::: {#0d173323 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import polars as pl graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]) .add_edges([("A", "B", 0.5), ("B", "C", 2.0), ("C", "A", 3.5)]) ) heavy = graph.get_edge_df().filter(pl.col("weight") > 1.0)["id"].to_list() graph.select_edges_by_id(heavy) graph.get_edge_df_ws() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
